title: Tulsi Ginger Tea

seo.title: Tulsi Ginger Tea for Cough and Congestion - Ayurvedic Home Remedy
seo.description: A simple Ayurvedic home tea of tulsi and ginger, taken warm, traditionally used to ease respiratory cough, sore throat and nasal congestion.

purpose: A warming household tea traditionally used to soothe cough, clear mild nasal congestion and support the throat during Kasa-Pratishyaya.
timing: Morning and evening, or when the throat feels irritated
anupana: Take warm. Optional 1/2 tsp honey after the tea has cooled slightly; never add honey to boiling liquid.
duration: 3-7 days for a mild seasonal cough, or as advised by a practitioner
traditional_context: Tulsi and ginger are classical Kapha-Vata pacifying kitchen herbs. Fresh tulsi leaves and ginger rhizome are simmered as a light decoction (kwatha-like tea) to kindle Agni, reduce Ama and ease Kasa and Pratishyaya. Honey, once the cup is warm rather than hot, is a traditional anupana for cough.

ingredients_list.quantity: 1-2 thin slices fresh, or a pinch of dry powder
ingredients_list.notes: Fresh ginger is preferred for a seasonal cough
Add only after the tea has cooled below steaming heat; never boil honey

preparation.step: Pour 1 to 1.5 cups of water into a small pan and add the tulsi leaves and ginger.
Bring to a gentle boil, then simmer for 5-8 minutes until the water is aromatic and slightly reduced.
Strain into a cup. Allow it to become comfortably warm.
If using honey, stir it in only after the tea has cooled below steaming heat. Sip slowly.

precautions.precaution: This is a kitchen support for mild seasonal cough, not a treatment for breathlessness, high fever or a cough lasting more than two to three weeks.
Do not give honey to infants under one year of age.
Stop if heartburn, mouth burning or allergy occurs.

who_should_avoid.warning: People with marked Pitta aggravation, active ulcers or severe reflux may find ginger-tulsi tea too heating.
Pregnant people, young children, and anyone on regular medicines should check with a qualified clinician before using it as a repeated remedy.
